blocks.text: Daniel 8 itself identifies the ram as Media-Persia and the goat as Greece. The later horn, whose actions include attacking the sanctuary, aligns most closely with Antiochus IV’s persecution; this does not justify mapping the vision with certainty onto present-day rulers, peoples, or states, or flattening Daniel’s little-horn imagery into a single timeless profile. Daniel 8 also begins the book’s return to Hebrew after the Aramaic section that began at 2:4b. That language pattern is important for reading the book’s structure, but it does not by itself establish when each section was written or prove a particular theory of composition.
